text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests ordered by a healthcare provider, such as the Mayo Clinic or via guidelines from MedlinePlus.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests ordered by a healthcare provider

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
Diabetes result: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after fasting (no food or drink except water) for at least 8 hours.
Diabetes result: 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher on two separate tests.

Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day, regardless of when you last ate. This is used if you already have classic symptoms of diabetes (such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss).
Diabetes result: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar before and 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes result: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher at the 2-hour mark.
Confirmation: Except in cases of clear random high blood sugar accompanied by classic symptoms, doctors usually confirm a diabetes diagnosis by repeating one of the tests on a different day.

Screening Recommendations: Routine screening is generally recommended for adults starting at age 35 (or age 45 by some guidelines), or earlier if you have risk factors like being overweight, physical inactivity, or a family history of diabetes. You can take an initial online check using the ADA Risk Test, though an official diagnosis requires lab work.
